objective: Resolve corpus population boundaries from the request context instead of categorically treating role, practice, portfolio, or primary-matter language as mere repository provenance.

evidence: attribution/C4/transition.json: the prior system-prompt edit was effective on its declared predictions but current traces show its categorical provenance rule overcorrected
changes.failure_pattern: Before searching, agents repeatedly discarded requested credentials, practice, portfolio, role, and primary-matter boundaries, then exhaustively reconciled and ranked an overbroad universe containing incidental references.
changes.mechanism: The always-visible protocol now distinguishes search-locus wording from contextual population qualifiers, rejects incidental-reference promotion unless the requested relationship permits it, and requires a boundary-candidate sensitivity test before ranking.
changes.rationale: Population interpretation is the earliest shared error and controls every later search and disposition; improving the partially successful C4 gate protocol is more direct than adding another reviewer after the universe is already wrong.

evidence: attribution/C4/transition.json: the prior reconciliation skill was partially effective at two of four predictions
changes.failure_pattern: The reconciliation procedure reinforced the overbroad population and lacked an operational comparison of plausible scope readings using role and purpose evidence for candidates at the boundary.
changes.mechanism: The registered skill adds context-sensitive population classes, a dedicated population/role evidence field, a mandatory changed-candidate boundary test, and a final audit that verifies the selected interpretation against engagement evidence.
changes.rationale: The skill owns the detailed candidate-ledger procedure and can operationalize the system-level semantic rule while preserving the useful C4 unread-file, proof-sufficiency, and symmetric-disposition checks.
